title: Cold rebuild: exactly the access CI needs
summary: Write a least-privilege Role and RoleBinding on a real Kubernetes cluster, from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a skill stuck. In *RBAC* you gave a CI service account exactly the access it needs in one namespace,
and proved it with `kubectl auth can-i`, on a real cluster. Now do it again from memory: the same scenario, **no
hints, no solution to peek at**. The checks are exactly the ones you passed the first time.
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old commands feels like knowing
them; doing it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: A RoleBinding in namespace `shop` refers to the ClusterRole `view`. What does the subject get?
options: Read access to most resources, but only in `shop`
steps.explain: This is the usual pattern: define a role once as a ClusterRole (`view`, `edit`, `admin` are built in) and bind it per namespace.

steps.title: Exactly the access CI needs, cold
prompt: This terminal runs a **real one-node Kubernetes 1.37 cluster** (k3s) with `kubectl` (alias `k`).
Create the ServiceAccount `ci-deployer` in `shop`, a Role `deployer` there that can get, list, watch, patch and update
Deployments and get and list pods (nothing else), and a RoleBinding that gives it to the ServiceAccount.
From memory: no hints this time.
